描述_ZN: Wisteria and Goldfish" scroll, painted by Xugu in the Qing dynasty, on paper with color, 125 cm in length and 66 cm in width.　　The picture depicts several goldfish swimming comfortably at the time when wisteria flowers are in full bloom. All of Xugu's paintings of wisteria and goldfish are titled "Golden Medallion with Purple Ribbon". The so-called "golden seal with purple ribbon" comes from the phrase "the ministerial state and the prime minister, both Qin officials, had golden seals and purple ribbons" in the Book of Han. These paintings are popular with the public for their auspicious symbolism of officialdom and prestige. The flowers and leaves of the wisteria in this painting are directly colored, and their fullness of moisture reveals their vivid vitality. The vines are expressed with intermittent and staccato sideways strokes, the strokes are broken but the air is continuous, forming an elegant rhythm of brushwork and ink. The form of the goldfish is simple and exaggerated, and although it is hastily made with red color, it is still moving and interesting. This painting shows the author's unique artistic charm with its clear and cool style.　　Signed: "Purple ribbon and gold seal. Written in honor of Lord Dianfu Fangbo. Xigu." Inscription: "Xugu" in vermilion.
